parts:
hi Manuel,
 there's no telling what the problem is here.
 For one thing you could check whether "K" has an effect on things by increasing its value.
 
 Secondly, I suggest simulating a data set exactly like yours (using the parameter values estimated from unmarked) and then fit that data set in unmarked and PRESENCE. That should diagnose if one or the other is in error.
 
 Of course we would all be interested to see the result!
andy

parts:
Hi Manuel, 

I just got the same results when fitting the model to the data used in the "Class6.R" script found here: https://sites.google.com/site/hierarchicalmodelingcourse/home/r-scripts. 


PRESENCE:
                                            estimate   std.error
A1     : p                                  0.157462 (0.085572)
A2     : lambda                            -0.172146 (0.080491)


unmarked
                Est         SE
p(Int)    0.1574618 0.08557164
lam(Int) -0.1721461 0.08049056


So, I can't replicate the problem. Did you by chance standardize covariates in unmarked, but not in PRESENCE? You should also use the same K as Andy suggested.

Richard

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Different results in unmarked and PRESENCE for Royle model
parts:
Hi Manuel,

I had the same issue, and I think it stems from the way the covariates are standardized in R vs Presence. If you use 'scale' in R, it yields different values than if you use 'Standardize covariate' in Presence (the 'Scale' option in Presence doesn't seem to do anything). Might also have something to do with the way you setup the Design Matrix in Presence?

Cheers,
Viorel

Hi Manuel,

I had the same issue, and I think it stems from the way the covariates are standardized in R vs Presence. If you use 'scale' in R, it yields different values than if you use 'Standardize covariate' in Presence (the 'Scale' option in Presence doesn't seem to do anything). Might also have something to do with the way you setup the Design Matrix in Presence?

Cheers,
Viorel

hi Manuel,
 there's no telling what the problem is here.
 For one thing you could check whether "K" has an effect on things by increasing its value.
 
 Secondly, I suggest simulating a data set exactly like yours (using the parameter values estimated from unmarked) and then fit that data set in unmarked and PRESENCE. That should diagnose if one or the other is in error.

andy
